standards.name: GIGW 3.0 (Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps)
IS 17802 (Part 1): 2021 — Accessibility for ICT products and services

criteria.title: Non-text Content
criteria.summary: Images, icons, charts and other non-text content have a text alternative that serves the same purpose. Decorative images are hidden from assistive technology.

criteria.title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Recorded audio-only content (such as a podcast) has a transcript. Recorded video without sound has a transcript or an audio track that describes it.

criteria.title: Captions (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Recorded videos with sound have accurate, synchronised captions.

criteria.title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Recorded videos have audio description, or a full text alternative that includes the important visual information.

criteria.title: Captions (Live)
criteria.summary: Live video with sound (for example webinars or AGM live streams) has real-time captions.

criteria.title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
criteria.summary: Recorded videos have audio description of important visual content that the soundtrack does not already convey.

criteria.title: Info and Relationships
criteria.summary: Structure shown visually (headings, lists, tables, form labels, groups of fields) is also present in the code, so assistive technology can convey it.

criteria.title: Meaningful Sequence
criteria.summary: The reading order in the code matches the meaningful visual order of the content.

criteria.title: Sensory Characteristics
criteria.summary: Instructions do not rely only on shape, colour, size, position or sound (for example "press the green button on the right").

criteria.title: Orientation
criteria.summary: Content works in both portrait and landscape orientation unless one orientation is essential.
affects: People whose device is mounted in a fixed orientation

criteria.title: Identify Input Purpose
criteria.summary: Fields that collect the user's own details (name, email, phone, address) use the correct autocomplete values, so browsers can fill them in.

criteria.title: Use of Color
criteria.summary: Colour is not the only way information is shown (for example errors, required fields, gains and losses, chart series, links within text).

criteria.title: Audio Control
criteria.summary: Audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds can be paused or stopped, or its volume changed separately from the system volume.

criteria.title: Contrast (Minimum)
criteria.summary: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, or 3:1 for large text.
affects: Anyone using a screen in bright light

criteria.title: Resize Text
criteria.summary: Text can be enlarged to 200% without losing content or functionality.

criteria.title: Images of Text
criteria.summary: Text is shown as real text, not as an image of text, except for logos or where the presentation is essential.
affects: People who change fonts or colours to read

criteria.title: Reflow
criteria.summary: Content fits a screen 320 CSS pixels wide (equivalent to 400% zoom) without scrolling in two directions, except content such as data tables, maps and charts.
affects: People with low vision who zoom

criteria.title: Non-text Contrast
criteria.summary: Form field borders, icons, focus indicators and the meaningful parts of charts have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colours.

criteria.title: Text Spacing
criteria.summary: No content or functionality is lost when users increase line, paragraph, letter and word spacing.

criteria.title: Content on Hover or Focus
criteria.summary: Tooltips and pop-ups that appear on hover or focus can be dismissed without moving focus, can themselves be hovered, and stay visible until dismissed.

criteria.title: Keyboard
criteria.summary: Everything can be operated with a keyboard alone.

criteria.title: No Keyboard Trap
criteria.summary: Keyboard focus can always be moved away from any component using the keyboard.

criteria.title: Character Key Shortcuts
criteria.summary: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off or remapped, or only work while the component has focus.

criteria.title: Timing Adjustable
criteria.summary: Users are warned before a time limit (such as a session timeout) expires and can extend it, unless the limit is essential or longer than 20 hours.

criteria.title: Pause, Stop, Hide
criteria.summary: Moving, blinking, scrolling or auto-updating content (tickers, carousels) that starts automatically and lasts more than 5 seconds can be paused, stopped or hidden.
affects: People with attention or cognitive disabilities

criteria.title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
criteria.summary: Nothing flashes more than three times in any one second.

criteria.title: Bypass Blocks
criteria.summary: Blocks repeated on every page can be skipped, for example with a "Skip to main content" link, headings or landmarks.

criteria.title: Page Titled
criteria.summary: Each page has a title that describes its topic or purpose.

criteria.title: Focus Order
criteria.summary: Keyboard focus moves through the page in an order that preserves meaning and use.

criteria.title: Link Purpose (In Context)
criteria.summary: The purpose of each link can be understood from its text, or from its text together with the surrounding sentence, list item or table cell.

criteria.title: Multiple Ways
criteria.summary: There is more than one way to find a page (for example navigation, search or a site map), except for steps in a process.

criteria.title: Headings and Labels
criteria.summary: Headings and labels describe the topic or purpose of the content they introduce.

criteria.title: Focus Visible
criteria.summary: The element that has keyboard focus has a visible focus indicator.

criteria.title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
criteria.summary: An element that receives keyboard focus is not completely hidden by other content, such as sticky headers, chat widgets or cookie banners.

criteria.title: Pointer Gestures
criteria.summary: Anything done with multi-finger or path-based gestures (pinch, swipe) can also be done with a single tap or click.

criteria.title: Pointer Cancellation
criteria.summary: Actions happen when the pointer is released, or can be aborted or undone, so accidental touches can be cancelled.

criteria.title: Label in Name
criteria.summary: The accessible name of a control contains the text shown on it, so speech-input users can say what they see.

criteria.title: Motion Actuation
criteria.summary: Anything triggered by moving the device (shake, tilt) can also be done through the interface, and the motion response can be turned off.

criteria.title: Dragging Movements
criteria.summary: Anything done by dragging (sliders, reordering) can also be done with single taps or clicks.

criteria.title: Target Size (Minimum)
criteria.summary: Click and tap targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or have enough space around them, with exceptions such as links inside sentences.

criteria.title: Language of Page
criteria.summary: The main language of each page is set in the code (for example lang="en" or lang="hi").

criteria.title: Language of Parts
criteria.summary: Passages in another language (such as Hindi or regional-language text on an English page) are marked with their own lang attribute so they are pronounced correctly.

criteria.title: On Focus
criteria.summary: Moving focus to a component does not by itself cause an unexpected change, such as submitting a form or opening a new window.

criteria.title: On Input
criteria.summary: Changing a setting (choosing an option, ticking a box) does not cause an unexpected change of context unless users were told beforehand.

criteria.title: Consistent Navigation
criteria.summary: Navigation repeated across pages appears in the same relative order each time.

criteria.title: Consistent Identification
criteria.summary: Components that do the same thing are identified the same way across the site (same labels and icons).

criteria.title: Consistent Help
criteria.summary: Help options repeated on several pages (contact details, chat, FAQ, grievance link) are in the same relative place on each page.

criteria.title: Error Identification
criteria.summary: When an input error is detected, the field in error is identified and the error is described in text.

criteria.title: Labels or Instructions
criteria.summary: Form fields have labels or instructions, including any required format (for example date of birth or PAN format).

criteria.title: Error Suggestion
criteria.summary: When an input error is detected and a correction is known, the suggestion is shown, unless that would compromise security.

criteria.title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
criteria.summary: For financial transactions, legal commitments and data changes (orders, fund transfers, KYC submissions), submissions can be reversed, are checked for errors, or can be reviewed and confirmed first.

criteria.title: Redundant Entry
criteria.summary: Information already entered in the same process is filled in automatically or offered for selection instead of being asked for again.

criteria.title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
criteria.summary: Signing in does not require a cognitive test (remembering a password, solving a puzzle or CAPTCHA) unless there is an alternative or help, such as allowing password managers and paste.

criteria.title: Parsing
criteria.summary: Obsolete in WCAG 2.2, which treats it as always satisfied for HTML content. Kept so WCAG 2.1 reports are complete.

criteria.title: Name, Role, Value
criteria.summary: Every control (buttons, links, form fields, custom widgets) has an accessible name and role, and its state and value are exposed to assistive technology.

criteria.title: Status Messages
criteria.summary: Status messages (such as "Order placed", search result counts or errors) are announced by assistive technology without moving focus.

gigw3.title: GIGW 3.0 (Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps)
gigw3.reviewNote: Placeholder requirements written from public summaries of GIGW 3.0. Requirement wording, numbering and mappings must be confirmed against the official GIGW 3.0 document by an IAAP-certified reviewer.

requirements.title: Websites and apps conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA
requirements.summary: GIGW 3.0 adopts WCAG 2.1 Level AA as its accessibility baseline.
steps: Complete the WCAG 2.1 AA manual tests for this property.
Confirm the conformance matrix shows no "Does not support" results.

requirements.title: An accessibility statement is published and linked from every page
requirements.summary: The site publishes an accessibility statement (commitment, standards, known limitations, contact for feedback) linked from a consistent place such as the footer.
steps: Find the accessibility statement link on the home page and two inner pages.
Check the statement names the standard, known limitations and a feedback contact.
Check the statement is dated and was reviewed in the last 12 months.

requirements.title: A "Skip to main content" link is provided
requirements.summary: Pages with repeated navigation start with a working "Skip to main content" link.
steps: Load a page and press Tab once; the first stop should be "Skip to main content".
Activate it and check focus moves past the navigation to the main content.

requirements.title: Content in Indian languages is marked up with the correct language
requirements.summary: Hindi and regional-language content uses the correct lang attribute, and language versions of pages are equivalent.
steps: Open each language version of the home page and check the page language is set.
Check passages in another language are marked with their own lang attribute.
Check the language versions offer the same information and services.

requirements.title: Downloadable documents are accessible
requirements.summary: PDFs and other documents (circulars, disclosures, forms, statements) are tagged and accessible, or an accessible alternative is offered.
steps: List the documents linked from the site (the scanner's "PDF links" finding helps).
Check a sample opens with a title, reading order, headings and table structure.
Check scanned-image PDFs have a text alternative.

requirements.title: CAPTCHA has an accessible alternative
requirements.summary: Any CAPTCHA offers an alternative, such as audio or a different verification method.
steps: Find every CAPTCHA (sign-in, registration, contact and grievance forms).
Complete each one with a screen reader and with the keyboard only.

requirements.title: Users can report accessibility problems and get a response
requirements.summary: A feedback or grievance mechanism for accessibility problems is available and monitored, with a stated response time.
steps: Find the accessibility feedback or grievance option from the home page.
Submit a test report and confirm it is acknowledged and tracked.

is17802.title: IS 17802 (Part 1): 2021 — Accessibility for ICT products and services
is17802.reviewNote: Placeholder requirements written from public summaries of IS 17802. Clause numbers, wording and mappings must be confirmed against the published standard by an IAAP-certified reviewer.

requirements.title: Web content requirements
requirements.summary: Requirements for web pages, expected to correspond to the WCAG 2.1 Level A and AA success criteria.
steps: Complete the WCAG 2.1 AA manual tests for this property.
Confirm the mapping to the standard's web clauses with the expert reviewer.

requirements.title: Non-web documents
requirements.summary: Requirements for documents such as PDFs (statements, contract notes, disclosures), expected to apply the WCAG criteria to documents.
steps: List the investor-facing documents (statements, contract notes, disclosures, forms).
Check a sample for tags, reading order, headings, table structure and alternative text.

requirements.title: Software and mobile apps
requirements.summary: Requirements for software, including mobile trading and investor apps. Android scanning arrives in a later phase; record manual results until then.
steps: Test the main app journeys (sign-in, KYC, orders, statements) with TalkBack.
Check text scaling to 200% and the app's behaviour in both orientations.

requirements.title: Documentation and support services
requirements.summary: Product documentation and support services (help pages, call centres, chat) offer accessible formats and communication methods.
steps: Check help and FAQ pages meet the web requirements.
Check support can be reached by at least one channel that does not require speech.

tools: Screen reader (NVDA on Windows or TalkBack on Android)
steps: List the images, icons, charts and image buttons on the page, including logos and icons inside links and buttons.
Check each informative image has alternative text that conveys the same information (for charts, the key figures or a nearby table).
Check icon-only buttons and links (search, menu, download) announce their purpose.
Check decorative images are silent in the screen reader (empty alt or hidden).
Check any CAPTCHA describes its purpose and offers a non-visual alternative.
Find recorded audio-only content (podcasts, recorded calls) and video-only content (silent animations).
Check audio-only content has a transcript with all spoken information.
Check video-only content has a transcript or an audio track describing the visual content.
Play each recorded video with sound, with captions turned on.
Check captions exist, are accurate and in sync, and include speaker changes and important sounds.
Check auto-generated captions have been reviewed (names, numbers and financial terms are correct).
Play each recorded video and note visual information not in the soundtrack (on-screen text, charts, actions).
Check that information is given in audio description or in a full text alternative next to the video.

tools: Live stream or recording of a past live event
steps: Identify live video with sound (webinars, AGM or results-call streams).
Check real-time captions are provided and reasonably accurate during the live event.
Play each recorded video and note visual information not in the soundtrack.
Check an audio-described version or audio description track conveys that information.

tools: Browser developer tools or an accessibility tree viewer
steps: Check visual headings are marked up as headings with levels that match the outline.
Check lists are marked up as lists, and data tables have header cells associated with data cells.
Check every form field is programmatically linked to its visible label, and related fields (date of birth, address, nominee details) are grouped with a legend.
Check required fields and instructions are conveyed in the code, not only visually.
Read the page with a screen reader from top to bottom.
Check the reading order makes sense, especially for multi-column layouts, cards and pop-ups.
Check hidden content does not interrupt the reading order.
Read the instructions on the page, including form and error instructions.
Check none rely only on shape, colour, size, position or sound (for example "click the green button" or "see the panel on the right").
Open the page on a mobile device in portrait, then rotate to landscape.
Check the content displays and works in both orientations, unless one is essential.
Find fields that collect the user's own details (name, email, mobile number, address, date of birth).
Check each has the correct autocomplete value (for example name, email, tel, street-address, bday).
Check the browser can autofill the fields.

tools: Colour blindness simulator (browser developer tools rendering options)
steps: Look for information conveyed by colour, such as errors, required fields, gains and losses, chart series, status badges, links in text.
Check each also uses text, an icon, a pattern or an underline.
Check with a greyscale or colour-blindness simulation that nothing is lost.
Load the page and listen for audio that starts automatically.
If audio plays for more than 3 seconds, check there is a control near the top of the page to pause, stop or change its volume.
Check text over images, gradients and videos, and text in images, which automated checks cannot measure.
Check placeholder text, disabled-looking text that is still meaningful, and text in hover and focus states.
Normal text needs 4.5:1; large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold) needs 3:1.
Zoom the browser to 200% on a desktop-sized window.
Check all text grows and no content is cut off, overlapped or hidden.
Check forms, menus and dialogs still work at 200%.
Look for images that contain text (banners, scanned notices, infographics, buttons drawn as images).
Check real text is used instead, unless it is a logo or the visual presentation is essential.

tools: Browser zoom or responsive mode set to 320 CSS pixels wide
steps: Set the window to 1280 pixels wide and zoom to 400% (or use a 320-pixel-wide viewport).
Check content reflows into one column with no horizontal scrolling, except for data tables, charts and maps.
Check nothing is cut off and all functions (menus, forms, dialogs) still work.
Check borders of form fields, checkboxes and radio buttons against the background (3:1).
Check icons that convey meaning and the focus indicator (3:1).
Check the lines and areas needed to understand charts (3:1 against adjacent colours).

tools: Text spacing bookmarklet or browser extension
steps: Apply line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2× font size, letter spacing 0.12× and word spacing 0.16×.
Check no text is cut off or overlaps, especially in buttons, tabs, cards and tables.
Find content that appears on hover or focus (tooltips, mega-menus, info icons).
Check it can be dismissed with Escape without moving the pointer or focus.
Check the pointer can move onto the new content without it disappearing.
Check it stays visible until dismissed or no longer relevant.
Put the mouse away and use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and the arrow keys.
Complete the main journeys (sign in, open an account or KYC step, place an order, download a statement, submit a grievance).
Check every link, button, menu, date picker, dropdown and custom widget works with the keyboard.
Tab through the whole page, including embedded content (videos, maps, chat widgets, iframes).
Check focus never gets stuck; for dialogs, check Escape or a close button returns focus.
Check documentation and settings for single-key shortcuts (letters, numbers, punctuation).
If any exist, check they can be turned off or remapped, or only work when the component has focus.
Sign in (with a test account) and stay idle until the session timeout.
Check a warning appears before expiry and lets the user extend the session with a simple action.
Check the warning is announced by a screen reader and gives at least 20 seconds to respond.
Check other time limits (OTP entry, order windows) can be extended or are essential.
Look for content that moves, blinks, scrolls or updates automatically (tickers, carousels, live prices).
If it starts automatically and lasts over 5 seconds, check it can be paused, stopped or hidden.
For auto-updating content, check users can pause or control how often it updates.

tools: Photosensitive epilepsy analysis tool for video content
steps: Look for flashing content in animations, banners and videos.
Check nothing flashes more than three times in any one second.
Press Tab once on a fresh page load; the first stop should be a "Skip to main content" link.
Activate it and check focus moves to the main content.
Check the page also has landmarks (header, navigation, main, footer) and headings.
Check the browser tab title of each page.
Check titles are unique and describe the page (for example "Open a demat account – Step 2 of 4 – Company").
Tab through the page and watch where focus goes.
Check the order follows the visual and logical order.
Check focus moves into dialogs when they open and returns to the trigger when they close.
Open the screen reader's list of links.
Check each link's purpose is clear from its text or its surrounding sentence, list item or table cell.
Check repeated "Read more", "Click here" or "Download" links can be told apart.
Check there are at least two ways to reach content pages, for example main navigation, search, site map or related links.
Steps in a process (such as KYC) are exempt.
Read each heading and check it describes the content that follows.
Read each form label and button and check it describes its purpose.
Tab through the page.
Check every focused element has a clearly visible focus indicator, including on dark backgrounds and in the header and footer.
Tab through the page with sticky headers, footers, cookie banners and chat widgets visible.
Check the focused element is never completely hidden by them.
Find features that use pinch, swipe or drawn gestures (carousels, charts, maps, signature pads).
Check each can also be done with single taps or clicks (buttons, controls).
Press down on buttons and links, then move the pointer away before releasing.
Check the action does not happen on press, or can be cancelled or undone.

tools: Screen reader or accessibility tree viewer
steps: Compare the visible text of buttons, links and labelled fields with their accessible names.
Check each accessible name contains the visible text, ideally at the start.
Look for features triggered by shaking or tilting the device.
Check they can also be done through on-screen controls and the motion response can be turned off.
Find features that use dragging (sliders for SIP amount or tenure, reorderable lists, maps).
Check each can also be done with single taps or clicks, such as plus and minus buttons or a text field.
Review findings from the automated target-size check.
Check small targets in custom components (icon buttons, pagination, close buttons) are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels or have enough spacing.
Check the html element's lang attribute matches the page's main language (for example "en" or "hi").
Check each language version of the site sets its own language.
Find passages in a different language from the page (Hindi or regional-language text on English pages, or English on Hindi pages).
Check each has its own lang attribute and the screen reader pronounces it correctly.
Tab through all controls.
Check focusing a control never submits a form, opens a new window, or moves focus unexpectedly.
Change every dropdown, radio button and checkbox.
Check none triggers navigation or submission unless users are told beforehand.
Compare the header, navigation and footer on several pages.
Check repeated navigation appears in the same relative order on each page.
Compare components that do the same thing across pages (search, download, help, print).
Check they use the same labels, icons and alternative text everywhere.
Find help options repeated on several pages (contact details, chat, FAQ, grievance link).
Check they appear in the same relative place on each page.
Submit each form with empty and invalid values.
Check each error identifies the field in text and describes the problem.
Check errors are announced by the screen reader, not shown only in colour.
Check every field has a visible label or instructions.
Check required fields and formats (PAN, IFSC, date of birth, mobile number) are stated before submission.
Submit forms with values in the wrong format.
Check the error suggests how to correct the value (for example "Enter PAN as 5 letters, 4 digits, 1 letter").
Go through journeys that create financial or legal commitments (orders, fund transfers, mandates, KYC submission, account changes).
Check users can review and confirm before submitting, or reverse the action, or that input is checked with a chance to correct it.
Go through multi-step processes (account opening, KYC, nominee addition).
Check information entered earlier is not asked for again, or is pre-filled or selectable.
Sign in with a password manager and check it can fill the username and password fields.
Check paste is allowed in password and OTP fields.
Check any CAPTCHA or puzzle has an alternative that does not require a cognitive test.
Use custom widgets (tabs, accordions, dropdowns, toggles, date pickers, dialogs) with a screen reader.
Check each announces its name, role and state (expanded, selected, checked) and announces changes.
Trigger status messages (add to watchlist, place an order, search results, form errors, loading states).
Check each is announced by the screen reader without moving focus.
